title: Product Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes - Inference Platform 2026
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Purpose
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, a high-level PRD and requirements, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the latest production release notes for Redwood Inference's core inference platform. Audience: product managers, engineering, go-to-market, solutions engineering, and customer success.

1) Product overview
-------------------
Short summary: Redwood Inference provides a unified inference platform for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with a focus on predictable latency, unit economics, and operations. The product offers: REST/SDK APIs for text generation, chat, embeddings; a model catalog; Dedicated GPU pools; Private VPC/on-prem installs; and a Console for observability and rollouts.
Key user personas:
- Application developers integrating LLM features (NLP engineers, backend engineers)
- Platform teams standardizing inference across orgs
- Enterprise security/compliance owners requiring VPC and audit controls

Outcomes we drive:
- Predictable latency SLOs (p99 < 300ms for short completion paths on Hosted for small models)
- Lower unit cost via batching/caching and quantization guidance (target 30% reduction for eligible workloads)
- Reduced operational burden for customers (self-serve rollouts, canaries, automatic fallback)

2) Product requirements (PRD) - high level
---------------------------------------
Scope: Improve platform capabilities to support large-scale, multi-tenant production workloads while reducing compute cost and improving reliability. Focus areas for next 6-12 months: routing & fallback policies, dynamic quantization profiles, improved Dedicated autoscaling, and first-class model evaluation hooks in the Console.

Success metrics (OKRs):
- Platform availability target: 99.95% for paid hosted endpoints
- End-to-end latency: p50/p95/p99 tracking per route; 10% improvement p95 vs baseline within 6 months
- Cost savings: average 20% unit-cost reduction across instrumented customers via Optimize recommendations
- Adoption: 30% of new customers enable Dedicated within 90 days when committed usage > $50k/month

User stories (representative):
1. As an app engineer, I want a canary rollout that routes 5% of traffic to a new model variant so I can validate quality before full rollout.
   - Acceptance criteria: configurable canary percentage, automatic metrics comparison (latency, cost, eval set quality), rollback on regression.
2. As an SRE, I want explicit capacity grace and burst policies for Dedicated so we avoid dropped requests during autoscaling.
   - Acceptance criteria: documented autoscaling policy, SLA for burst capacity, observability dashboards and alerts.
3. As a security officer, I want VPC-only control plane options and KMS integration for Private installs.
   - Acceptance criteria: documented deployment checklist, KMS/HSM integration guide, audit log retention options.

Non-functional requirements:
- Multi-region routing with regional failover latency penalty <= 200ms additional RTT on failover
- Per-route token quotas enforced at ingress with <50ms enforcement latency
- Rolling upgrades with zero data-plane downtime for minor revisions
- Telemetry ingestion: 100% of production requests report minimal traces and cost tokens for billing reconciliation

3) Design spec (high-level)
---------------------------
Architecture overview:
- Control plane: hosted service (multitenant) that manages config, model catalog, routing policies, and billing.
- Data plane: inference runtime deployed on GPU pools (Dedicated/Hosted) with a lightweight agent for Private installs.
- Smart router: policy engine that routes by latency SLO, cost target, region, model compatibility; supports automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- Caching layer: prefix/KV cache at the data plane for KV-cacheable models; per-tenant cache TTL and size quotas.

Key components and interactions:
- API Gateway -> Router -> Serving Runtime -> GPU worker pool / cache.
- Console interacts with Control Plane for rollouts and with runtime via tracing hooks for request-level diagnostics.

API surface (examples)
- POST /v1/generate
  - body: {"model": "redwood-v1-small", "input": "...", "max_tokens": 128, "client_metadata": {"route": "chat-1"}}
- POST /v1/rollouts/canary
  - body: {"model": "mymodel:2", "percent": 5, "compare_metrics": ["latency_p95","eval_quality"]}

Configuration examples (YAML)
- canary_policy:
    percent: 5
    compare_metrics: ["eval_quality","latency_p95"]
    rollback_on: ["eval_quality_drop>2%","latency_p95_increase>15%"]

Operational concerns and SLOs
- SLOs: 99.95% availability (monthly), latency targets tracked per route, error budget allocation per customer tier.
- Monitoring: per-route dashboards (p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, throughput), alert thresholds: p95 latency increase >20% for 10m or error rate >1% for 5m.

Security and privacy
- Data-in-flight encryption (TLS 1.3), customer-managed keys for Private deployments, audit logs with immutable storage option.
- PII handling: recommend prompt redaction for sensitive fields; provide built-in redaction templates in Console.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 4 quarters)
------------------------------------
Themes by quarter (high level):
- Q2 2026: Routing & resiliency: multi-model fallback, regional failover, canary automation.
- Q3 2026: Cost optimization: automated quantization rollout, Optimize suggestions in Console, cold-start reductions.
- Q4 2026: Enterprise readiness: Private on-prem packaging, enhanced KMS/HSM integrations, compliance evidence automation.
- Q1 2027: Developer experience & evals: first-class eval sets in Console, prompt-store, integrated quality guardrails.

Milestones and owners:
- Canary automation MVP (ship): 2026-05-30, owner: Eng-Platform (PM: Jordan Lee).
- Quantization pipeline (beta): 2026-08-15, owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime (PM: Priya Kapoor).
- Private packaging v1 (GA): 2026-11-01, owner: Eng-Private-Deployments (PM: Marcus Silva).

Cross-team dependencies:
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: quantization kernel selection and validation harness.
- Eng-SRE: autoscaling policies and capacity planning for Dedicated.
- Security & Compliance: evidence templates for SOC/ISO audits.

5) Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for go-to-market)
------------------------------------------------------
Offer tiers (recommended):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation pricing + per-embedding pricing. Base tier includes standard models and shared capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual committed spend with discounted per-token rates and guaranteed throughput. Includes baseline burst buffer.
- Private (enterprise): platform license + deployment fee + optional managed services. Pricing quoted per-customer.

Suggested pricing bands (example, public-facing guidance):
- Hosted generation: $0.012 / 1k tokens (small models), $0.045 / 1k tokens (large models)
- Embeddings: $0.0025 / embedding (base models)
- Dedicated reserve: commit starting at $10k/month for small pool; discounts 20-45% depending on commitment term
- Optimize add-on: $X/month or % of spend for proactive recommendations and higher retention of telemetry.

Packaging considerations:
- Feature gating: Dedicated & Private customers get advanced autoscaling controls, higher retention for logs, and enterprise SLA.
- Trials: 30-day credits for Dedicated evaluation; credit-sized Dedicated pools for POC.
- Bundle: offer Console-Plus (advanced evals + rollout automation) as paid add-on.

Billing & metering notes:
- Meter at token-granularity with reconciliation keys for customer billing.
- Include cost attribution in Console with per-route, per-model token breakdown.

6) Release notes (latest stable release)
---------------------------------------
Release: inference-platform v1.8.0 (2026-02-20)
Highlights:
- Canary Rollouts (Beta): support for percent-based canaries with automatic metric comparison and rollback triggers.
- Quantized variant routing: Smart router can now fall back to quantized variants under capacity pressure, reducing costs.
- Dedicated autoscale improvements: faster scale-up path (avg 40% reduction in cold-start latency), new burst buffer config.
- Console: new per-route cost breakdown and token-level query explorer.

Bug fixes and minor improvements:
- Fixed a race condition in KV cache eviction that could cause duplicate responses under high load.
- Improved telemetry fidelity for token accounting in multi-part requests.
- Various UI/UX polish to rollout pages and model catalog.

Upgrade notes and rollback plan:
- Rolling upgrade across control plane instances; data plane workers receive a rolling restart with drain period of 60s.
- Rollback: toggle model routing to previous variant using Console -> Rollouts -> Rollback. For embedded Dedicated/private customers, follow the runbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback.

7) Rollout & launch checklist (for PMs/Eng/Vendors)
---------------------------------------------------
Pre-launch:
- QA: e2e test suite green, load test at 1.5x target traffic.
- Security: SCA/pen test completed, KMS integration smoke tests.
- Documentation: API docs updated, SDKs released, migration guide published.

Launch:
1. Enable canary for small percentage (5%).
2. Monitor roll-forward metrics for 1h.
3. Gradually increase to 25% over 2h if stable.
4. Full rollout and announcement.

Post-launch:
- Monitor error budget, latency, and cost signals for 72h.
- Customer outreach to early adopters with feedback form.

10) Appendix: example evaluation criteria for canary
---------------------------------------------------
- Metric window: compare 30m baseline vs 30m canary after stabilization period.
- Pass criteria: no increase >10% in latency_p95, eval_quality delta <= 1% (customer provided eval set), error rate <= 0.5% absolute increase.
- Auto-rollback triggers: eval_quality_drop >2% OR latency_p95 increase >15% for sustained 5m.
